incidents.summary: BAE Systems agreed to £287 million in US and UK criminal penalties and was convicted in the US of felony conspiracy to defraud the government.

sources.title: BAE Systems
sources.quote: On 5 February 2010, BAE Systems agreed to pay criminal fines of £257 million (US$400 million) to the US and £30 million to the UK.

sources.title: BAE Systems
sources.quote: The $400 million fine was a result of a plea bargain with the US Department of Justice (DOJ) whereby BAE Systems was convicted of felony conspiracy to defraud the United States government.

sources.title: BAE Systems
sources.quote: The report, Ethical business conduct in BAE Systems plc – the way forward, made 23 recommendations, measures which the company committed to implement.

incidents.summary: BAE Systems' US subsidiary agreed to a $36 million settlement over 104 violations of US arms export restrictions between 2019 and 2025.

sources.title: The Morning Risk Report: BAE Systems Fined $36 Million for Illegal Exports - WSJ
sources.quote: Good morning. BAE Systems is set to pay $36 million for violating U.S. export restrictions on military technology.

sources.title: The Morning Risk Report: BAE Systems Fined $36 Million for Illegal Exports - WSJ
sources.quote: A U.S. subsidiary of the U.K.-based defense manufacturer was charged with violating U.S. arms trafficking regulations 104 times between 2019 and 2025, according to the settlement.

sources.title: BAE Systems to pay $36m penalty after 104 violations of US arms export rules | BAE Systems | The Guardian
sources.quote: BAE voluntarily disclosed all but one of the alleged violations by its US arm.

incidents.summary: The Australian National Audit Office found that BAE overstated the development level of its Hunter-class frigate design, contributing to underestimated cost inflation and schedule slippage.

sources.title: SINKING BILLIONS – UNDERGUNNED AND OVERPRICED - Declassified Australia
sources.quote: The Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) reported in May its findings on the multi-billion dollar contract Australia signed in December 2018 with BAE Systems to build nine Hunter-class frigates.

sources.title: SINKING BILLIONS – UNDERGUNNED AND OVERPRICED - Declassified Australia
sources.quote: ANAO found that BAE had ‘over-stated’ – bureaucrat language for lied – the level of development of the frigate’s design, which meant cost inflation and schedule slippage were severely under-estimated.

incidents.summary: EnComm Aviation sued BAE Systems for £120 million over its withdrawal of support for aircraft used to deliver humanitarian aid.

sources.title: BAE faces £120m lawsuit over decision to scrap support for aid aircraft | Global development | The Guardian
sources.quote: Britain’s biggest weapons manufacturer, BAE Systems, is facing a £120m lawsuit after scrapping support for aircraft used to deliver aid to some of the world’s neediest countries.

sources.title: BAE faces £120m lawsuit over decision to scrap support for aid aircraft | Global development | The Guardian
sources.quote: The Kenya-based operator is suing BAE for effectively grounding its fleet.

incidents.summary: Open burning of hazardous production waste at the BAE-operated Radford plant drew community concern, while a replacement incinerator was delayed until summer 2026.

sources.title: Incinerator Project Continues at RAAP – News Journal
sources.quote: Officials from the plant and the government contractor which runs the local facility, BAE Systems, updated the public this past week during an online community meeting.

sources.title: Incinerator Project Continues at RAAP – News Journal
sources.quote: The propellant production results in waste containing various hazardous chemicals, such as barium, chromium, and mercury. The practice has been to simply burn the waste at the OBG.

sources.title: Incinerator Project Continues at RAAP – News Journal
sources.quote: Initially, the project had been expected to be completed by this year, but now is scheduled for a summer of 2026 date.

positives: University of Sheffield researchers collaborated with BAE Systems and AMRC North West to establish a life-cycle environmental assessment framework for fast jets, focusing on Scope 3 emissions.
